questions.solution:
Given integration is

${∫}_{3\sqrt{2}4}^{3\sqrt{3}4}\dfrac{48}{9 - 4x^{2}}dx$

We know that

$∫ \dfrac{dx}{a^{2} - x^{2}} = \sin^{- 1}\dfrac{x}{a} + C$

So, the equation can be re-written as

${∫}_{3\sqrt{2}4}^{3\sqrt{3}4}\dfrac{48}{2\sqrt{\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)2 - x^{2}}}dx = \dfrac{48}{2} \times {\sin^{- 1}\dfrac{2x}{3}}_{3\sqrt{2}4}^{3\sqrt{3}4}$

$= 24 \times \left[\sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{4}\right) - \sin^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{3\sqrt{2}}{4}\right)\right]

$= 24 $\times\left[\sin^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right) - \sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\right]

$= 24 \times \left[\dfrac{π}{3} - \dfrac{π}{4}\right] ==$2\pi$

questions.q: The value of $\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}\dfrac{\sin^{3}x}{\sin x + \cos x}dx$ is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{\sin^{3}x}{\sin x + \cos x}dx . . . \left(i\right)$

Using property of definite integration ${∫}_a^{b}f\left(x\right)dx = {∫}_a^{b}f\left(a + b - x\right)dx,$ we get

$I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{\sin^{3}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - x\right)}{\sin \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - x\right) + \cos \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - x\right)}dx$

Using $\sin \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - x\right) = \cos x \text{ and } \cos \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - x\right) = \sin x,$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{\cos^{3}\left(x\right)}{\cos \left(x\right) + \sin \left(x\right)}dx . . . \left(ii\right)$

On adding the equation $\left(i\right) \text{ and } \left(ii\right)$

$⇒ 2I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{\sin^{3}x + \cos^{3}x}{\sin x + \cos x}dx$

$⇒ 2I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{\left(\sin x + \cos x\right)\left(\sin^{2}x + \cos^{2}x - \sin x \cos x\right)}{\sin x + \cos x}dx$

$⇒ 2I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left(\sin^{2}x + \cos^{2}x - \sin x \cos x\right)dx$

Now, using $\sin^{2}x + \cos^{2}x = 1 \text{ and } 2\sin x \cos x = \sin 2x,$ we get

$⇒ 2I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{2}\sin 2x\right)dx$

$⇒ 2I = {\left[x + \dfrac{\cos 2x}{4}\right]}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}$

$⇒ 2I = \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} + \dfrac{\cos 2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}{4}\right) - \left(0 + \dfrac{\cos 2\left(0\right)}{4}\right)$

$⇒ 2I = \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{1}{4}\right) - \left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)$

$⇒ 2I = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{\pi - 1}{4} .$
questions.question: The value of $\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}\dfrac{\sin^{3}x}{\sin x + \cos x}dx$ is:
questions.explanation:
$I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{\sin^{3}x}{\sin x + \cos x}dx . . . \left(i\right)$

Using property of definite integration ${∫}_a^{b}f\left(x\right)dx = {∫}_a^{b}f\left(a + b - x\right)dx,$ we get

$I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{\sin^{3}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - x\right)}{\sin \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - x\right) + \cos \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - x\right)}dx$

Using $\sin \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - x\right) = \cos x \text{ and } \cos \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - x\right) = \sin x,$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{\cos^{3}\left(x\right)}{\cos \left(x\right) + \sin \left(x\right)}dx . . . \left(ii\right)$

On adding the equation $\left(i\right) \text{ and } \left(ii\right)$

$⇒ 2I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{\sin^{3}x + \cos^{3}x}{\sin x + \cos x}dx$

$⇒ 2I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{\left(\sin x + \cos x\right)\left(\sin^{2}x + \cos^{2}x - \sin x \cos x\right)}{\sin x + \cos x}dx$

$⇒ 2I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left(\sin^{2}x + \cos^{2}x - \sin x \cos x\right)dx$

Now, using $\sin^{2}x + \cos^{2}x = 1 \text{ and } 2\sin x \cos x = \sin 2x,$ we get

$⇒ 2I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{2}\sin 2x\right)dx$

$⇒ 2I = {\left[x + \dfrac{\cos 2x}{4}\right]}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}$

$⇒ 2I = \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} + \dfrac{\cos 2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}{4}\right) - \left(0 + \dfrac{\cos 2\left(0\right)}{4}\right)$

$⇒ 2I = \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{1}{4}\right) - \left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)$

$⇒ 2I = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{\pi - 1}{4} .$

questions.q: Let  \left[t\right]$~denote the greatest integer less than or equal to $t$. Then the value of the integral ${∫}_{- 3}^{101}\left(\left[\sin \left(\pix\right)\right] + e\left[\cos \left(2\pix\right)\right]\right)dx$& is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,& ${∫}_{- 3}^{101}\left(\left[sin\pix\right] + e\left[\cos 2\pix\right]\right)dx$

Now let~${I}_{1} = {∫}_{- 3}^{101}\left[sin\pix\right]dx$~and~${I}_{2} = {∫}_{- 3}^{101}e \left[\cos 2\pix\right]dx$

Now checking periodicity of~\left[sin\pix\right]$~we get,

$0 < x < 1 ⇒ \left[sin\pix\right] = 0$

$1 < x < 2 ⇒ \left[sin\pix\right] = - 1$

\left[sin\pix\right] \to$ periodic with period 2

So,~${I}_{1} = 52{∫}_{0}^{2}\left[sin\pix\right]dx$

$= 52\left[{∫}_{0}^{1}0 + {∫}_{1}^{2} - 1dx\right] = - 52$

Now checking periodicity of~ \left[\cos 2\pix\right]$~we get,

$0 < x < \dfrac{1}{4} ⇒ \left[\cos 2\pix\right] = 0$

$\dfrac{1}{4} < x < \dfrac{1}{2} ⇒ \left[\cos 2\pix\right] = - 1$

$\dfrac{1}{2} < x < \dfrac{3}{4} ⇒ \left[\cos 2\pix\right] = - 1$

$\dfrac{3}{4} < x < 1 ⇒ \left[\cos 2\pix\right] = 0$

So,~\left[\cos 2\pix\right]$~has periodicity of~$1$

So,~${I}_{2} = 104 \left({∫}_{0}^{14}e^{0}dx + {∫}_{14}^{34}e^{- 1}dx + {∫}_{34}^{1}e^{0}dx\right)$

$⇒ {I}_{2} = 104 \left(\dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{e} \times \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{4}\right)

$⇒ {I}_{2} = 52 + $\dfrac{52}{e}

So,~${I}_{1} + {I}_{2} = $\dfrac{52}{e}~or~${∫}_{- $3}^{101}\left(\left[$sin\pix\right] + $e\left[$\cos 2\pix\right]\right)dx = $\dfrac{52}{e}

$

questions.q: Let $f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}e^{t}f  \left(t\right)dt + e^{x}$ be a differentiable function for all $x \in R$. Then $f\left(x\right) equals :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& $f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}e^{t}f\left(t\right)dt + e^{x} ⇒ f\left(0\right) = 1$

Differentiating with respect to $x$~we get,~

$f^{'}\left(x\right) = e^{x}f \left(x\right) + e^{x}$

$f^{'}\left(x\right) = $e^{x}\l$left(f\left($x\right) + 1)$

$\dfrac{f^{'}\left(x\right)}{f\left(x\right) + 1} =e^{x}$

Integrate both the sides we get,~

${∫}_{0}^{x}\dfrac{f^{'}\left(x\right)}{f\left(x\right) + 1}$dx = {∫}_{0}^{x}e^{x}dx$

{ln\lleft(f\left(x\right) + 1)}_{0}^{x}{= e^{x}}_{0}^{x}$

ln\l$left(f\left($x\right) + 1) - $ln\lleft(f\left(0\right) + 1) = e^{x} - 1$

$\ln \left(\dfrac{f\left(x\right) + 1}{2}\right) =e^{x} - 1$ ~ {as f\left(0\right) = 1}$

$f\left(x\right) = 2e\left(e^{x} - 1\right) - 1

$

questions.q: Let ${I}_{n}\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}\dfrac{1}{\left(t^{2} + 5\right)n}dt, n = 1, 2, 3, \ldots .$ Then
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

${I}_{n}\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}\dfrac{dt}{\left(t^{2} + 5\right)n}$

Applying integration~by parts we get,

$⇒ {I}_{n}\left(x\right) = {\dfrac{t}{\left(t^{2} + 5\right)n}}_{0}^{x} - {∫}_{0}^{x}n\left(t^{2} + 5\right)- n - 1 \cdot 2t^{2}$

$⇒ {I}_{n}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x}{\left(x^{2} + 5\right)n} + 2n{∫}_{0}^{x}\dfrac{t2}{\left(t^{2} + 5\right)n + 1}dt$

$⇒ {I}_{n}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x}{\left(x^{2} + 5\right)n} + 2n{∫}_{0}^{x}\dfrac{\left(t^{2} + 5\right) - 5}{\left(t^{2} + 5\right)n + 1}dt$

$⇒ {I}_{n}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x}{\left(x^{2} + 5\right)n} + 2n{∫}_{0}^{x}\dfrac{dt}{\left(t^{2} + 5\right)n} - 10n{∫}_{0}^{x}\dfrac{dt}{\left(t^{2} + 5\right)n + 1}$

$⇒ {I}_{n} \left(x\right) = $\dfrac{x}{ \left(x^{2} + 5\right)n}$ +2n{I}_{n}\left(x\right) - 10n{I}_{n + 1}\left(x\right)$

$⇒ 10n{I}_{n + 1}\left(x\right) + \left(1 - 2n\right){I}_{n}\left(x\right) = $\dfrac{x}{\left(x^{2} + 5\right)n}

$⇒ 10n{I}_{n + 1}\left(x\right) + \left(1 - 2n\right){I}_{n}\left(x\right) = xI^{'}n$~{where $I^{'}n = $\dfrac{1}{\left(x^{2} + 5\right)n}~we get by differentiating~${I}_{n}\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}\dfrac{dt}{\left(t^{2} + 5\right)n}}

Now put $n = 5$

We get,~$50{I}_{6} - 9{I}_{5} = x{I}_{5}^{'}$

$

questions.q: If for all real triplets \left(a, b, c\right), f\left(x\right) = a + bx + cx^{2};$ then $\mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}f\left(x\right)dx$ is equal to:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
${\mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\left\left(a + bx + cx^{2}\right)dx = ax + \dfrac{bx^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{cx^{3}}{3}\right|}_{0}^{1} = a + \dfrac{b}{2} + \dfrac{c}{3}$

$f\left(1\right) = a + b + c$

$f\left(0\right) = a$

$f\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = a + \dfrac{b}{2} + \dfrac{C}{4}$

Now

$\dfrac{1}{6}\left(f\left(1\right) + f\left(0\right) + 4f\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\right) = \dfrac{1}{6}\left(a + b + c + a + 4\left(a + \dfrac{b}{2} + \dfrac{c}{4}\right)\right) = \dfrac{1}{6}\left(6a + 3b + 2c\right) = a + \dfrac{b}{2} + \dfrac{c}{3}$

questions.q: If $( a, b )$ be the orthocentre of the triangle whose vertices are $( 1, 2 ) , ( 2, 3 )$ and $( 3, 1 )$, and ${I}_{1} = {∫}_a^{b}xsin\left(4x - x^{2}\right)dx, {I}_{2} = {∫}_a^{b}\sin \left(4x - x^{2}\right)dx$ , then $36\dfrac{I1}{I2}$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Equation of $CE$ is given by,

$⇒ \left(y - 1\right) = $\dfrac{- 1}{\dfrac{3 - 2}{2 - 1}}\left($x - 3\right)$

$⇒ \left(y - 1\right) = - ( x - 3 )$

$⇒ x + y = 4 . . . \left(i\right)$

Similarly, equation of $AD$ is given by,

$⇒ \left(y - 2\right) = $\dfrac{- 1}{\dfrac{3 - 1}{2 - 3}}\left($x - 1\right)$

$⇒ \left($y - 2\right) = $\dfrac{1}{2}\left($x - 1\right)$

$⇒ 2y - 4 = x - 1$

$⇒ x - 2y + 3 = 0$

Using \left($i\right)$

$⇒ 4 - y - 2y + 3 = 0$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{7}{3}$

$⇒ x = 4 - \dfrac{7}{3}$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{5}{3}$

So, Orthocentre is $H ≡ \left(a, b\right) = \left(\dfrac{5}{3}, \dfrac{7}{3}\right).

Orthocentre lies on the line $x + y = 4$

So, $a + b = 4$

Now, ${I}_{1} = {∫}_a^{b}xsin ( x ( 4 - x ) ) dx . . . ( 1 )$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = {∫}_a^{b} ( a + b - x ) \sin ( \left($a + b - x\right) ( 4 - \left($a + b - x\right) ) ) dx$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = {∫}_a^{b} ( 4 - x ) \sin ( x ( 4 - x ) ) dx . . . ( 2 )$

Using, $( 1 ) + ( 2 )$

$⇒ 2{I}_{1} = {∫}_a^{b}4\sin ( x ( 4 - x ) ) dx$

$⇒ 2{I}_{1} = 4{I}_{2}$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = 2{I}_{2}$

$⇒ $\dfrac{I1}{I2} =$2$

$⇒ $\dfrac{36{I}_{1}}{I2} =$72

$

questions.q: Let $f\left(x\right) = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{x}g\left(t\right)dt,$ where $g$ is a non-zero even function. If $f\left(x + 5\right) = g\left(x\right),$ then $\mathop{∫}_{0}^{x}f ( t ) dt$ equals

questions.solution:

$f\left(x\right) = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{x}g ( t ) dt$ will be an odd function,
$⇒ f \left(-x\right) = - f \left(x\right)$
Let $I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{x}f\left(t\right)dt$ put $t = z + 5$
$⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_{- 5}^{x - 5}f\left(z + 5\right)dz$
$⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_{- 5}^{x - 5}g ( z ) dz \left($∵ f \left($x + 5\right) = g \left(x\right)\right)$
$⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_{- 5}^{x - 5}f^{'} ( z ) dz ( ∵ f^{'} ( x ) = g ( x ) )$
$⇒ I = f ( z ) {|}_{- 5}^{x - 5} = f ( x - 5 ) - f \left(-$5\right)$
$⇒ I = f ( 5 ) - f \left($5 + x\right)$ ( $f$ is~an odd function and $g$~is~given as an even~function)
$⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_{5 + x}^{5}f^{'} ( t ) dt =\mathop{∫}_{5 + x}^{5}g ( t ) dt$

questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}e^{x - t}f^{'}\left(t\right)dt - \left(x^{2} - x + 1\right)e^{x}$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = e^{x}{∫}_{0}^{x}e^{- t}f^{'}\left(t\right)dt - \left(x^{2} - x + 1\right)e^{x}$

$⇒ e^{- x}f \left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}e^{- t}f^{'}\left(t\right)dt - \left(x^{2} - x + 1\right)$

Differentiate on both side w.r.t~$x$~we get,

$e^{- x}f^{'}\left(x\right) + $\l$left(-f\left($x\right)e^{- x}) = e^{- x}f^{'} \left($x\right) - 2x + 1$

$⇒ $f\left($x\right) = $e^{x}\left($2x - 1\right)$

$⇒ f^{'} \left($x\right) = e^{x} \left(2\right) + e^{x}\left(2x - 1\right)$

$⇒ f^{'} \left(x\right) = e^{x} \left($2x + 1\right) . . . . . . \left($1\right)$

Now finding critical point we get,

$2x + 1 = 0 ⇒ x = - \dfrac{1}{2}$

Now differentiating equation~ \left(1\right)$~to check maxima and minima we get,

$f^{"}\left(x\right) = e^{x} \left(2\right) + \left($2x + 1\right)e^{x}$

$⇒ f^{"}\left($x\right) = $e^{x}\left($2x + 3\right)$

For $x = - $\dfrac{1}{2},$f^{"}\left(\dfrac{-1}${2}\right) > 0$, so it will give point of~ minima,

Now minimum value will be given by,~f\left(\dfrac{- 1}{2}\right) =$e^{- $\d$dfrac{1}{2}}\left(-$1 - 1\right) = - \dfrac{2}{e}$

questions.q: Let& $\alpha > 0$. If ${∫}_{0}^{α}\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{x + \alpha} - \sqrt{x}}dx = \dfrac{16 + 20\sqrt{2}}{15}$~then $\alpha$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

${∫}_{0}^{α}\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{x + \alpha} - \sqrt{x}}dx = \dfrac{16 + 20\sqrt{2}}{15} . . . . ( 1 )$

Rationalise the denominator in L.H.S we get,

${∫}_{0}^{α}\dfrac{x ( \sqrt{\alpha + x} + \sqrt{x} )}{α}dx = \dfrac{1}{α} \left[{∫}_{0}^{α}}x\sqrt{\alpha +$x}$dx + {∫}_{0}^{α}x^{3 / 2}dx\right]$

Put~\alpha +$x = t^{2} ⇒ dx = 2tdt$

Limit when~$x = 0 \to t = \sqrt{\alpha},x = $\alpha \tot = $\sqrt{2\alpha}$

$\dfrac{1}{α}{∫}_{\alpha}^{2\alpha} \left($t^{2} - \alpha\right)2t^{2}dt + $\dfrac{2{α}^{3 / 2}}{5}

=\dfrac{1}{α}{\dfrac{2t^{5}}{5} - \dfrac{2\alphat^{3}}{3}}_{\alpha}^{2\alpha} + \dfrac{2{α}^{3 / 2}}{5}

=\dfrac{4\alpha\sqrt{2\alpha} + 10\alpha\sqrt{\alpha}}{15}

From equation~ \left($1\right)$

${∫}_{0}^{α}\ddfrac{x}{\sqrt{x + \alpha} - \sqrt{x}}$dx = $\dfrac{16 + 20\sqrt{2}}{15}

$⇒ $\dfrac{4\alpha\sqrt{2\alpha} + 10\alpha\sqrt{\alpha}}{15} = \dfrac{16 + 20\sqrt{2}}{15}

On comparing both sides we get,

\alpha =$2$

questions.q: The value of the integral ${∫}_{0}^{1}x\cot^{- 1}\left(1 - x^{2} + x^{4}\right)dx$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given integral,& $I = {∫}_{0}^{1}x\cot^{- 1}\left(1 - x^{2} + x^{4}\right)dx$

Put $x^{2} = t, ⇒ 2xdx = dt$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}\cot^{- 1}\left(1 - t + t^{2}\right)dt$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{1 - t + t^{2}}\right)dt$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{t - \left(t - 1\right)}{1 + t\left(t - 1\right)}\right)dt$

Using~$\tan^{- 1}a - \tan^{- 1}b = \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{a - b}{1 + a \cdot b}\right),$~we get

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2} \left[{∫}_{0}^{1} \left(\tan^{- 1}$t\right)dt - {∫}_{0}^{1}\tan^{- 1}$\left($t - 1\right)dt\right]$

Using~${∫}_a^{b}f\left($x\right)dx = {∫}_a^{b}f\left($a + b - x\right)dx,$~we get

$⇒ I = $\dfrac{1}{2}\left[{∫}_{0}^{1} \left(\tan^{- 1}$t\right)dt - {∫}_{0}^{1}\tan^{- 1}\left(\left($1 - t\right) - 1\right)dt\right]$

$⇒ I = $\dfrac{1}{2} \left[{∫}_{0}^{1} \left(\tan^{- 1}t\right)dt - {∫}_{0}^{1}\tan^{- 1}\left(-t\right)dt\right]$

Now, using~$\tan^{- 1}\left(-a\right) = - \tan^{- 1}a,$~we get

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2} \left[{∫}_{0}^{1}\left(\tan^{- 1}$t\right)dt + {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(\tan^{- 1}$t\right)dt\right]$

$⇒ I = $\dfrac{1}{2} \left[$2{∫}_{0}^{1}\tan^{- 1}tdt\right]$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{1}\left($1 ⋅ \tan^{- 1}t\right)dt$

Now applying the integration by parts i.e.~${∫}_a^{b}\left($u \cdotv\right)dx = u{∫}_a^{b}vdx - {∫}_a^{b}\left[\d$dfrac{d}{dx}\left($u\right) ∫ vdx\right]dx + c$

$⇒ I = {\tan^{- 1}t ⋅ t |}_{0}^{1} - {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(\dfrac{1}{1 + t^{2}}⋅ t\right)dt$

Put~$1 + t^{2} = u, ⇒ 2tdt = du$

$⇒ I = \tan^{- 1}$ \left(1\right) ⋅ 1 - 0 - \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{1}^{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{u}\right)du$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{π}{4} - \dfrac{1}{2}\log_{2}\left(u\right){}_{1}^{2}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{π}{4} - \dfrac{1}{2}\log_{\mathrm{e}}2 .$

$

questions.q: If ${I}_{m, n} = {∫}_{0}^{1}x^{m - 1}\left(1 - x\right)n - 1dx$, for $m, n ⩾ 1$, and ${∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{x^{m - 1} + x^{n - 1}}{\left(1 + x\right)m + n}dx = \alpha{I}_{m, n}, \alpha \in R$, then~$\alpha$& equals ________.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
${I}_{m, n} = {∫}_{0}^{1}x^{m - 1}\left(1 - x\right)n - 1dx = {I}_{n, m}$

Now Let $x = \dfrac{1}{y + 1} ⇒ dx = - \dfrac{1}{\left(y + 1\right)2}dy$

So,~${I}_{m, n} = - {∫}_{∞}^{0}\dfrac{1}{\left(y + 1\right)m - 1}\dfrac{yn - 1}{\left(y + 1\right)n - 1}\dfrac{dy}{\left(y + 1\right)2} = {∫}_{0}^{∞}\dfrac{yn - 1}{\left(1 + y\right)m + n}dy$

similarly ${I}_{m, n} = {∫}_{0}^{∞}\dfrac{ym - 1}{\left(1 + y\right)m + n}dy$

Now $2{I}_{m, n} = {∫}_{0}^{∞}\dfrac{y^{m - 1} + y^{n - 1}}{\left(1 + y\right)m + n}dy$

$= {∫}_{0}^{∞}\dfrac{y^{m - 1} + y^{n - 1}}{\left(1 + y\right)m + n}dy$

$= {∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{y^{m - 1} + y^{n - 1}}{\left(1 + y\right)m + n}dy + \mathop{{∫}_{1}^{∞}\dfrac{y^{m - 1} + y^{n - 1}}{\left(1 + y\right)m + n}dy ⏟}_{substitutey = \dfrac{1}{t}}$

$⇒ 2{I}_{m, n} = {∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{y^{m - 1} + y^{n - 1}}{\left(1 + y\right)m + n}dy - {∫}_{1}^{0}\dfrac{t^{n - 1} + t^{m - 1}}{tm + n - 2}\dfrac{tm + n}{\left(1 + t\right)m + n}\dfrac{dt}{t2}$

$⇒$ Hence $2{I}_{m, n} = 2{∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{y^{m - 1} + y^{n - 1}}{\left(1 + y\right)m + n}dy ⇒ \alpha = 1$

questions.q: If ${∫}_{13}^{3} \left|\log_{\mathrm{e}}$x\right|dx = $\dfrac{m}{n}\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(\dfrac{n2}{e}\right), where $m$ and $n$ are coprime natural numbers, then $m^{2} + n^{2} - 5$ \text{ and } is equal to _____ .$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let

$I = {∫}_{13}^{3}\left|\ln x\right|dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{13}^{1}\left|\ln x\right|dx + {∫}_{1}^{3}\left|\ln x\right|dx$

$⇒ I = - {∫}_{13}^{1}lnxdx + {∫}_{1}^{3}lnxdx$

Since,~$\ln x < 0forx \in \left(0, 1\right)$.

$⇒ I = - {xlnx - x}_{13}^{1} + {xlnx - x}_{1}^{3}$

$⇒ I = - \left[\left(0 - 1\right) - \left(- \dfrac{1}{3}\ln 3 - \dfrac{1}{3}\right)\right] + \left[3\ln 3 - 3 - \left(0 - 1\right)\right]$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{2}{3} - \dfrac{1}{3}\ln 3 + 3\ln 3 - 2$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{8}{3}\ln 3 - \dfrac{4}{3}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{4}{3} \left(2\ln 3 - 1\right)$

$⇒ I = $\dfrac{4}{3} \left(ln{3}^{2} - lne\right)$

$⇒ I = $\dfrac{4}{3}$\ln \left(\dfrac{32}{e})$

So,~$m = 4, n = 3$

Hence,~$m^{2} + n^{2} - 5 = 16 + 9 - 5 = 20$

$

questions.q: If $f(t)=\int_0^\pi \frac{2 x \mathrm{~d} x}{1-\cos ^2 \mathrm{t} \sin ^2 x}, 0 \lt \mathrm{t} \lt \pi$, then the value of $\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \frac{\pi^2 \mathrm{dt}}{f(\mathrm{t})}$ equals_________
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$f(t)=\int_0^\pi \frac{2 x}{1-\cos ^2 t \sin ^2 x} d x$ .....(1)
$=2 \int_0^\pi \frac{(\pi-x) d x}{1-\cos ^2 \sin ^2 x}$ .....(2)
$\begin{aligned}
& 2 f(t)=2 \int_0^\pi \frac{\pi}{1-\cos ^2 \sin ^2 x} d x \\
& f(t)=\int_0^\pi \frac{\pi}{1-\cos ^2 t \sin ^2 x} d x
\end{aligned}$
divide \& by $\cos ^2 \mathrm{x}$\begin{aligned}
& f(t)=\pi \int_0^\pi \frac{\sec ^2 x d x}{\sec ^2 x-\cos ^2 t^2 x} \\
& f(t)=2 \pi \int_0^{\pi / 2} \frac{\sec ^2 x d x}{\sec ^2 x-\cos ^2 t^2 \tan ^2 x} \\
& \tan x=z \\
& \sec ^2 x d x=d z \\
& f(t)=2 \pi \int_0^{\infty} \frac{d z}{1+\sin ^2 t \cdot z^2} \\
& =\frac{\pi^2}{\sin t}
\end{aligned}$$
Then $\int_0^{\pi / 2} \frac{\pi^2}{f(t)} d t$\begin{aligned}
& =\int_0^{\pi / 2} \sin t d t \\
& =1
\end{aligned}$$

questions.q: Let& $f$~be a twice differentiable function on~$R$. If~$f^{'}\left(0\right) = 4$~and~$f\left(x\right) + {∫}_{0}^{x}\left(x - t\right)f^{'}\left(t\right)dt$~$= \left(e^{2x} + e^{- 2x}\right)\cos 2x + \dfrac{2}{a}x$, then~\left(2a + 1\right)5a^{2}$ \text{ and } is equal to _______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) + {∫}_{0}^{x} \left($x - t\right)f^{'} \left(t\right)dt = \left($e^{2x} + e^{- 2x}\right)\cos 2x + \dfrac{2x}{a}⋯ \left($i\right)$

Putting~$x = 0$~both side we get,~$f \left($0\right) = 2 ⋯ \left($ii\right)$

On differentiating equation~ \left(i\right)$~w.r.t.~$x$~we get:

$f^{'}\left(x\right) + {∫}_{0}^{x}f^{'}\left(t\right)dt + xf^{'}\left(x\right) - xf^{'}\left(x\right) = 2\left(e^{2x} - e^{- 2x}\right)\cos 2x - 2\left(e^{2x} + e^{- 2x}\right)\sin 2x + \dfrac{2}{a}$

$⇒ f^{'}\left(x\right) + f\left(x\right) - f\left(0\right) = 2\left(e^{2x} - e^{- 2x}\right)\cos 2x - 2\left(e^{2x} + e^{- 2x}\right)\sin 2x + \dfrac{2}{a}$

Replace~$x$~by~$0$~we get:

$⇒ 4 = \dfrac{2}{a}⇒ a = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Now putting the value of~$a$~$in\left(2a + 1\right)5 \cdota^{2}$

We get,~${2}^{5} \cdot \dfrac{1}{22} = {2}^{3} =8

$

questions.q: The value of $b > 3$~for which $12{∫}_{3}^{b}\dfrac{1}{ \left(x^{2} - 1\right)\left(x^{2} - 4\right)}$dx = \log_{\mathrm{e}} \left(\dfrac{49}{40}\right),$is equal to _____. \text{ and } $
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given $12 \times {∫}_{3}^{b}\dfrac{1dx}{\left(x^{2} - 4\right)\left(x^{2} - 1\right)} = \ln \left[\dfrac{49}{40}\right] \text{ and } 4b > 3$

$⇒$ By Using partial fraction

$\dfrac{1}{ \left(x^{2} - 4\right) \left(x^{2} - 1\right)} = \dfrac{1}{3} \left(\dfrac{1}{x^{2} - 4} - \dfrac{1}{x^{2} - 1}\right)

$⇒ $\dfrac{12}{3}{∫}_{3}^{b} \left[\dfrac{1}{x^{2} - 4} - \dfrac{1}{x^{2} - 1}\right] =\ln \left(\dfrac{49}{40}\right)

$⇒ $4{\dfrac{1}{4}\log \left(\dfrac{x - 2}{x + 2}\right) - \dfrac{1}{2}\text{ log } \left(\dfrac{x - 1}{x + 1}\right)}$_{3}^{b} = $\ln \left(\dfrac{49}{40}\right)

$⇒ $\log \left(\dfrac{\left(b - 2\right) \left(b + 1\right)2}{\left(b + 2\right)\left(b - 1\right)2}$$\times \dfrac{5}{4}) ===log\dfrac{49}{40}

$⇒ $\dfrac{\left(b - 2\right)\left(b + 1\right)2}{ \left(b + 2\right) \left(b - 1\right)2}$ $\times $\dfrac{5}{4} = \dfrac{49}{40}

$⇒ $\dfrac{\left(b - 2\right) \left(b + 1\right)2}{ \left(b + 2\right)\left($b - 1\right)2} = \dfrac{49}{50} . . . \left($i\right)$

Comparing by hit and trial and taking~\left(b + 1\right)2 = 49 ⇒ b + 1 = 7 ⇒ b = 6$~

Now putting~$b = 6$~in equation (i) to corsscheck,

we~get~\dfrac{4 \times {7}^{2}}{8 \times {5}^{2}} = \dfrac{49}{50}~which is true~

So~$b = 6$~ is correct option,

Hence~$b = 6$
